issues.problem: The canonical Kitsu domain has moved to kitsu.app; kitsu.io is the legacy domain and may only work through redirection.
issues.suggestion: Use https://kitsu.app/api/edge and update the example to the same domain.

issues.problem: Kitsu documents the OAuth2 password and refresh-token grants. Client-credentials authentication is not documented, and self-service application registration is explicitly not implemented.
issues.suggestion: State that authenticated access uses the password grant at /api/oauth/token followed by a Bearer token; remove the client-credentials and account-settings registration claims.

issues.problem: curl interprets square brackets as URL globbing even inside quotes, so filter[text] can produce a bad-range error.
issues.suggestion: Use curl -s 'https://kitsu.app/api/edge/anime?filter%5Btext%5D=cowboy%20bebop' -H 'Accept: application/vnd.api+json', or add --globoff.

issues.problem: https://api.kraken.com is only the host, while the documented Spot REST base is https://api.kraken.com/0. It also does not cover the derivatives APIs claimed in the description; Kraken Futures uses separate futures.kraken.com roots.
issues.suggestion: Set the base URL to https://api.kraken.com/0 and scope the entry to Spot REST, or separately document Futures roots such as https://futures.kraken.com/derivatives/api/v3.

issues.problem: artist.getInfo returns the artist play count under stats.playcount, not stats.plays.
issues.suggestion: Replace "plays":"1599101" with "playcount":"1599101".

issues.problem: The value is an unfilled schema placeholder rather than an API URL.
issues.suggestion: Use https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0 for the current supported production API version.

issues.problem: The value is an unfilled schema placeholder.
issues.suggestion: Use the current Launch Library 2 documentation at https://ll.thespacedevs.com/ or the official overview at https://thespacedevs.com/llapi.

issues.problem: Unauthenticated access is available, but higher-limit API keys are offered to project supporters; the claim that a token follows a free signup is unsupported.
issues.suggestion: State that no authentication is needed for the public allowance and that higher-rate API keys are available through The Space Devs' Patreon/supporter program.

issues.problem: The value is an unfilled schema placeholder despite a published limit.
issues.suggestion: Set it to 15 unauthenticated calls per hour; the development endpoint has stale/limited data but no rate limit.

issues.problem: null omits the publicly offered supporter access for higher rate limits.
issues.suggestion: Mention that higher-rate API keys are available through The Space Devs' Patreon tiers; verify the selected tier's current allowance before publishing exact numbers.

issues.problem: The value is an unfilled schema placeholder.
issues.suggestion: Use 15 calls per hour for unauthenticated production requests and note that authenticated supporter limits vary by tier.

issues.problem: Both the request and response are unfilled schema placeholders.
issues.suggestion: Use a real example such as curl -s 'https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/upcoming/?limit=1', with a response shaped like {"count":...,"next":...,"previous":null,"results":[...]}.

issues.problem: The value is an unfilled schema placeholder.
issues.suggestion: Describe it as The Space Devs' API for launches, events, agencies, astronauts, stations, spacecraft, and related spaceflight data.

issues.problem: LaunchDarkly's REST API expects the token itself in the Authorization header. The documented REST examples do not prefix it with Bearer; doing so can make authentication fail.
issues.suggestion: Use Authorization: YOUR_API_KEY and remove the claimed Bearer alternative.

issues.problem: The current documented limit is 300 API calls per minute, not 120. The documentation identifies X-Ratelimit-Limit and X-Ratelimit-Remaining headers but does not promise Retry-After.
issues.suggestion: Set this to 300 calls per minute; successful responses include X-Ratelimit-Limit and X-Ratelimit-Remaining, and excess requests return 429.

issues.problem: The phrase "plus payment processing" double-counts the standard fee: Lemon Squeezy describes its base 5% + $0.50 platform fee as covering payment processing and other merchant-of-record costs, with specific surcharges in some cases.
issues.suggestion: State that the standard platform fee is 5% + $0.50 per transaction, with possible international, PayPal, subscription, affiliate, and other surcharges; custom pricing is available.

issues.problem: The documented User object does not have a status attribute. It instead includes fields such as color, avatar_url, has_custom_avatar, createdAt, and updatedAt.
issues.suggestion: Remove "status":"active" and use attributes from the documented User schema.

issues.problem: The claimed typical allowance of 20–30 requests per second conflicts with Lichess's published guidance to make only one request at a time and, after a 429, wait a full minute.
issues.suggestion: State that fixed limits are intentionally unpublished; send one request at a time and pause for one minute after any 429 response.

issues.problem: The provider website is currently returning an error and is not the effective subscription/reference surface for this RapidAPI-hosted interface.
issues.suggestion: Use the current RapidAPI listing, https://rapidapi.com/rokish/api/lingua-robot, as the documentation and subscription URL unless the provider site becomes reliable again.

issues.problem: Pricing is not unknown: RapidAPI currently publishes a Basic free plan with 2,500 requests per day and paid Pro, Ultra, and Mega plans.
issues.suggestion: Set the free limit to 2,500 requests/day and record the currently published $10, $49, and $99 monthly tiers, including their overage and bandwidth charges.

issues.problem: Rate limits are published through the plan quotas rather than being wholly unpublished.
issues.suggestion: Record the plan-based daily request allowances: 2,500/day on Basic, 25,000/day on Pro, 250,000/day on Ultra, and 2,500,000/day on Mega, subject to rechecking RapidAPI pricing.

issues.problem: The entry treats the legacy /v2 path as the universal LinkedIn API root. Current versioned product APIs generally use https://api.linkedin.com/rest with a LinkedIn-Version header, while certain endpoints such as OIDC /v2/userinfo remain exceptions.
issues.suggestion: Use https://api.linkedin.com/rest for current versioned APIs and explicitly document https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo as a legacy-path OIDC exception rather than one universal base.

issues.problem: LinkedIn's OIDC UserInfo examples use a BCP 47 locale such as en-US, not en_US.
issues.suggestion: Change "locale":"en_US" to "locale":"en-US".
